Report Text:
Anatomic Site: frontal lobe lesion
Recurrent oligodendroglioma vs treatment effect
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 52-year-old female with grade II oligodendroglioma status post radiotherapy. She presents for surgical resection.
Gross Description:
The specimen is received fresh in three parts, each labeled with the patient's name and medical record number.
Part A is labeled "frontal lobe lesion." It comprises multiple soft tissue fragments, measuring 3.0 x 2.5 x 1.0 cm in aggregate. The tissue is predominantly tan-pink with areas of dark-brown discoloration. A portion is used for cytologic preparation, with the remaining tissue submitted entirely in cassettes A1 through A3.
Part B is labeled "necrotic tissue." It consists of a single fragment of mottled brown and tan tissue, measuring 2.5 x 1.5 x 0.8 cm. The cut surface reveals a mixture of necrotic and viable tissue. The specimen is bisected and submitted in cassettes B1 and B2.
Part C is labeled "recurrent oligodendroglioma vs treatment effect." It consists of a single unoriented fragment of tan and red-brown tissue, measuring 2.8 x 2.3 x 1.5 cm. Cut sections show central necrosis with surrounding hemorrhage and inflammation. The specimen is entirely submitted in cassettes C1 and C2.
Diagnosis Comments:
No infiltrative glioma is identified in Parts A-C. Immunohistochemical studies were performed to evaluate this case.
- GFAP: Positive in reactive astrocytes.
- IDH1: Negative.
- Ki-67: Low proliferative index.
Interoperative Diagnosis:
FS1 (A) Brain, "frontal lobe lesion," excision: Cortex with reactive changes and necrosis, consistent with treatment effect.
Final Diagnosis:
A. Brain, "frontal lobe lesion," resection: Cortex and white matter with reactive and dystrophic changes; no infiltrative glioma identified.
B. Brain, "necrotic tissue," biopsy: Segment of cortex with necrotic and hemorrhagic changes.
C. Brain, "recurrent oligodendroglioma vs treatment effect," resection: Extensive necrosis and hemorrhage; no infiltrative glioma identified.

Anatomic Site: temporal lobe mass
Tumor
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 37-year-old male with a previously diagnosed anaplastic oligodendroglioma, WHO grade III, presenting for resection.
Gross Description:
The specimen is received fresh in two parts, each labeled with the patient's name and medical record number.
Part A, labeled 'tumor,' consists of a single fragment of tan-white brain tissue (0.7 x 0.6 x 0.4 cm). A portion of the specimen is taken for frozen section diagnosis, with the remnant submitted in cassette A1. The non-frozen portion is submitted in cassette A2.
Part B, labeled 'tumor,' consists of multiple, soft, pink-yellow, irregular unoriented tissue fragments (2.0 x 0.7 x 0.3 cm in aggregate). The specimen is entirely submitted in cassette B1.
Interoperative Diagnosis:
FS1 (A) Brain, biopsy: Consistent with anaplastic oligodendroglioma, WHO grade III.
Final Diagnosis:
A. Brain, temporal lobe, biopsy: Anaplastic oligodendroglioma, WHO grade III.
B. Brain, temporal lobe, resection: Anaplastic oligodendroglioma, WHO grade III.

Anatomic Site: occipital lobe tumor
Suspicion of recurrence
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 45-year-old female with a history of oligodendroglioma, WHO grade II, status post chemotherapy.
Gross Description:
The specimen is received fresh in four parts, each labeled with the patient's name and medical record number.
Part A is labeled "occipital lobe tumor." It consists of multiple fragments of soft tissue, measuring 2.9 x 2.2 x 0.8 cm in aggregate. The specimen is tan-pink with areas of hemorrhage. A portion is used for frozen section diagnosis, and the remaining tissue is submitted in cassettes A1 through A3.
Part B is labeled "tumor bed." It consists of a single unoriented fragment of tan tissue with brown mottling, measuring 3.2 x 1.7 x 1.1 cm. The cut surface shows tan tissue with areas of necrosis. The specimen is bisected and submitted in cassettes B1 and B2.
Part C is labeled "suspicion of recurrence." It consists of a single unoriented fragment of pink-tan tissue with brown discoloration, measuring 2.5 x 2.1 x 1.4 cm. The cut sections show predominantly brown tissue with central necrosis. The specimen is entirely submitted in cassettes C1 and C2.
Diagnosis Comments:
Each part of this case (Parts A-C) has been submitted in their entirety for evaluation. No definitive infiltrative glioma is identified.
Immunohistochemical studies were performed:
- Synaptophysin: Negative.
- Olig2: Positive.
- Ki-67: Less than 5%.
Interoperative Diagnosis:
FS1 (A) Brain, "occipital lobe tumor," excision: Cortex with treatment effect and reactive changes.
Final Diagnosis:
A. Brain, "occipital lobe tumor," biopsy: Cortex with reactive and dystrophic changes; no infiltrative glioma identified.
B. Brain, "tumor bed," resection: Cortex with necrotic tissue; no definitive glioma identified.
C. Brain, "suspicion of recurrence," resection: Extensive necrosis and hemorrhage; no infiltrative glioma identified.
